name: r10_shell_bottom_moves
why: IT IS THE CASE. A hollowed box, a blind hole in the bottom, and the box becomes taller. The bottom still exists -- no face disappears -- but it has moved by 28 mm. A hole anchored to where the bottom was before ends up in the void, and the part comes out different from the confirmed one.
intent_why: «the hole in the bottom» means in the bottom. The box is open underneath and the bottom is the ceiling, 5 thick: raising it from 52 to 80 the bottom goes from z = 47 to z = 75. A hole that stays at absolute z is no longer in the bottom, and there is no longer any material there to remove.

after.tolerance_why: the shell alone has its centroid at 57.443; the hole (z 75..78, centre 76.5) takes it to 57.253. If the hole stayed where it was, at z 47..50, it would be in the VOID and would remove nothing: 57.443. One hundred and ninety thousandths between the two answers, and five hundredths of tolerance tell them apart. THE VOLUME IS NOT USED ON PURPOSE: the shell that SOLIDWORKS builds has 960 mm3 more than the nested-boxes model (measured), and that 960 has nothing to do with the hole -- an expectation on the absolute volume would misclassify the case because of an error in MY calculation, not in the part
